_about: Cross-claims the layers standing check accepts (tests/layersStanding.test.ts): a layered row of <category> that <claimed_by>'s mapping also places by a SKU rule. Each group is recorded with its exact row count — a new group, a grown or shrunk count, or a stale entry fails the check. Statuses: claimant-rule-too-broad (fix in that category's round), decided-home (a decision placed the family here), pending-round (the home is decided in the named round), pending-decision:Q-<n> (kept where filed while that open question is answered — re-audit decisions, operator, 15 Sep 2026, F-6; the status is stale once the question closes).

SM-71XX-BLANK is the blank panel of the Cisco 7100 VPN router, placed in routers by that platform's own SKU rule; it arrived from security with the move of 16 Sep (run #1150, a 7100 part filed under FirePOWER 7000). The interfaces-modules SM- rule reads any SM- PID that is not an SM-X, an SRE or a disk, so it also claims this one: one home per SKU, and the home is routers (implementer, operator's 12-hour delegation, 16 Sep 2026)

passive CWDM mux / demux / OADM plug-ins and their chassis, which the transceiver -> optical-networking move of 16 Sep (run #1167) put in optical-networking, where the CWDM mux series holds them; the transceiver CWDM rule matches any CWDM- PID that is not a GBIC, so it also claims them — one home per SKU, and the home is optical-networking (implementer, operator's 12-hour delegation, 16 Sep 2026)

TWO DECISIONS MET HERE AND THE LATER ONE STANDS. The interfaces-modules round (14 Sep 2026, item 7) gave every NIM / SPA / EPA / HWIC / PVDM / VIC / SM-X card one home, interfaces-modules, and its plan ran (run #1068). The re-audit then planned the ASR 1000-ONLY SPAs back to routers under A.3 rule 1 (a card bound to one platform lives with its platform), and that plan ran on 16 Sep (run #1174). So these three rows sit in routers, placed by the ASR 1000 series rule, while the interfaces-modules ^SPA- rule still claims every SPA- PID: one home per SKU, and the home is routers. The operator may prefer the earlier blanket rule — it is a question about the SPA family, not about these rows' placement (implementer, operator's 12-hour delegation, 16 Sep 2026)
